chapter_note: The chapter preserves a three-name cosmological teaching about the First Man ('approved', 'righteous', 'only begotten') in ¶3–5, which is genuine substrate — systematic, impersonal explanation of cosmic epithets with both mapping sides staying within the cosmic system (aeons of light, the enemy, the Father, five sons). Paragraph 8 contains a substrate description of the First Man's cosmic function (standing firm in Darkness, purifying, freeing). The editorial layer then applies these cosmic attributes to the community (¶6, ¶9–10), with ¶4 showing institutional vocabulary ('catechumen') inserted into substrate teaching. Heavy lacunae throughout limit confidence. Gardner's synopsis confirms the Christological/exhortative editorial purpose. Moderate editorial fatigue with exhortation surging in the second half.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.285⟩[ ... ] and the [righte]o[usness ... ] is more than [the ... ] the voice through them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extremely fragmentary. Mentions 'righteousness' which connects to the chapter's three-name teaching about the First Man. No editorial markers present. Tentatively substrate but classification is very uncertain due to lacunae.

'The apostle speaks to them about these four...' is formulaic dialogue-frame attribution. The reference to 'these four' might gesture at substantive content but is too fragmentary to extract. 'Because they had recounted to him from [the hour] and time' is narrative framing.

paragraphs.core_text: This one, whom they called "approved" [ ... ... ] they approved him in the midst of the ae[ons of] light. These numerous multitudes set him a[part], and he came forth against the enemy. They gave this name [ ... ... ] this matter [ ... ... ] who are numerous, that are in the aeons of light and who [are without] measure or number.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First element of a three-name cosmological teaching (approved, righteous, only begotten). Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system: the aeons of light approve the First Man and set him apart against the enemy. Systematic, impersonal, expository. Classic substrate structure.

paragraphs.core_text: This one, [whom they called] "righteous", because he is the first righteous one who had no sin amongst all of the aeons that belong to the light and the thought [ ... ] they knew him, so that [ ... becau]se he is the first [wh]o obe[y]ed his Father, who had sent him with five sons [ ... ] perdition.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional term 'catechumen' from 'he is the first catechumen [wh]o obe[y]ed his Father' — editor projects the Manichaean institutional category of catechumen onto the cosmic figure of the First Man. This is a single-word institutional insertion into otherwise continuous substrate teaching.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second element of the three-name teaching. The substrate describes the First Man as 'righteous' — without sin among the aeons of light, obeying his Father, sent with five sons (the five elements). The institutional vocabulary 'catechumen' (flagged at 4.92) is a clear editorial gloss: the editor maps the cosmic obedience of the First Man onto the institutional role of catechumen. 'Five sons' is core Manichaean cosmological nomenclature for the First Man's emanations.

paragraphs.core_text: This one also [whom they called] "only begotten", because he was established [ ... ] pour [ ... ] enemy.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third element of the three-name teaching. Very fragmentary but the naming formula ('This one also [whom they called]') and the cosmological content (established against the enemy) match ¶3 and ¶4 exactly. Both sides stay within the cosmic system.

Clear pivot to application: 'So now, I tell you, my brothers and my limbs' — classic exhortation formula. The three cosmic names (approved, righteous, only begotten) are now applied to the community: 'after the likeness of the First Man.' One side of the mapping leaves the cosmic system and reaches into the editor's community. Contains institutional vocabulary 'catechumen' (×2). Exhortation score 5.71 confirms. This is where cosmos→cosmos mapping becomes cosmos→community application.

paragraphs.core_text: [the o]nly begot-ten also from gold and silver and all the [ ... ] of the universe.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed applicative framing: 'Again, just as the only begotten ones from your [only] begotten race and you [ ... ] according to flesh [ ... ... ]' — editorial comparison structure ('just as... your race... you') that applies the cosmic teaching to the community audience.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Very fragmentary. The gold and silver reference is a potential metal-body correspondence (substrate marker: metal mapped to cosmic being). 'Only begotten from gold and silver and all the [...] of the universe' appears to describe the cosmic constitution of the First Man or light beings. However, this is wrapped in applicative framing ('your race,' 'you,' 'according to flesh'). Low confidence in extraction due to heavy lacunae.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.286⟩ [The F]irst Man, himself stood firm in the [midst] of all the worlds of Darkness. He did not love [the] worlds of Darkness, nor did he lust for them! Rather, h[is] thought and love for the household of his people is in h[i]m. Anything else that the enemy [ ... ] with his violent de[e]ds. Behold, (the First Man) toils and struggles; so that (the enemy) would be separat[e from] them and be cast out from them. And he purifies them and ma[ke]s them f[r]ee, and makes them as they were from the beginning.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed applicative framing: 'Just as your father,' — editorial address that sets up the comparison for ¶9's 'You too...' application. The 'Just as' connects the cosmic description to the exhortation that follows.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Strong substrate content: the First Man standing firm in the worlds of Darkness, not loving them, his thought directed to his people, toiling against the enemy, purifying and freeing, restoring to the original state. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system — this describes WHAT the First Man IS and DOES. The 'your father' address and 'Just as' comparative structure are editorial framing that prepare for the application in ¶9. Capitalized 'Darkness' as it names the cosmic realm/entity.

'You too, so long as you stand firm' — direct application of the First Man's cosmic steadfastness to the community. 'After the likeness of your living father' explicitly marks this as imitation-teaching. The cosmic mapping now reaches outside the system to address the audience's behavior in 'this body.'

Continues the applicative voice. 'May they discover the remembrance of the household of his people' — the cosmic concept ('household of his people' from ¶8) is now being applied devotionally. 'Night and day' is temporal rather than cosmological. Fragmentary but consistent with the exhortative closure pattern.

Formulaic closing: disciples hear, rejoice, give glory, praise, make obeisance. Editorial seam correctly flagged — bridge connective with institutional vocabulary ('teacher,' 'disciples'). Classic dialogue-frame closure that wraps the teaching session. The structure flag 'formulaic closing' at the chapter level confirms this.
